public_rationale: The sources document concentration concerns and vulnerability to disappointed AI expectations. They do not establish one of history's largest speculative equity overvaluations at publication. An earlier peer-reviewed study also found no bubble in several major technology companies under its method. These records neither prove nor decisively refute the complete causal and historical claim.
limitations: All cited market assessments precede the target window and are context only.
Bubble detection and historical rankings depend on the chosen valuation method.
Concentration is not itself proof of mispricing.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The hypotheticals of the AI industry have created one of the largest equities bubbles in modern history, concentrated in a handful of AI-trade names.

statement.excerpt: The theoreticals and hypotheticals of this industry are so powerful that they’ve created one of the (if not the) largest equities bubbles in modern history, all heavily-centralized around the valuations of a handful of names related to the so-called AI trade, which translates to “buying or selling stuff to do with AI GPUs.”

from_speaker: created one of the (if not the) largest equities bubbles in modern history
heavily-centralized around the valuations of a handful of names
buying or selling stuff to do with AI GPUs
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that speculative AI expectations have materially inflated equity values beyond reasonable earnings prospects, with the excess concentrated in a small group of AI-related companies.
Large market capitalization or concentration alone does not establish a bubble.
The historical ranking requires comparable measures of speculative overvaluation, rather than simply comparing nominal market capitalization across decades.
The contemporaneous market-state window is the last completed trading session before publication and the publication day, October 19–20, 2026. The drafting time is unknown.
No numerical rank is imposed on 'one of the largest'; a decisive conclusion would need to remain credible across reasonable historical measures.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable historical analysis establishes an exceptionally large speculative equity overvaluation in the contemporaneous AI trade, concentrated in a small group of companies, and evidence attributes a material part of that overvaluation to AI expectations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Robust contemporaneous evidence shows that the claimed speculative overvaluation is absent, is not historically exceptional, or is not materially attributable to AI expectations. A different conclusion under one model alone is insufficient.

evidence.explanation: The report supports the concentration concern in an earlier market snapshot. It does not establish that October valuations constituted one of history's largest bubbles.

evidence.excerpt: No bubble detected for Apple, Microsoft, and Amazon.
evidence.explanation: This study found different bubble-test results across large technology companies. It cautions against treating all large AI-linked valuations as speculative, but its earlier sample and particular method cannot disprove the October claim.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A contemporaneous, reproducible historical comparison of speculative overvaluation, together with evidence identifying the contribution of AI expectations and the concentration of that excess.
